theme: Regional macro for LatAm and APAC: Mexico INEGI/Banxico, Brazil IBGE/BCB, Argentina INDEC, Colombia DANE, Chile, Japan e-Stat, Korea KOSIS, Australia ABS, India MOSPI clients
queries_run: gh search repos "inegi api python" --sort stars
gh search repos "ibge api" python --sort stars
gh search repos "e-stat" japan api --sort stars
gh search repos "australian bureau of statistics" api --sort stars
gh search repos "dane colombia api" OR "indec argentina api" OR "mospi india" --sort stars

candidates.name: nowcasting-mexico
candidates.what_it_holds: Reproducible nowcasting pipeline for Mexican economic activity (IGAE) combining Google Trends, mobility data, and the Banxico SIE API. Implements AR, DFM, MIDAS, LASSO, Ridge, Random Forest with pseudo out-of-sample evaluation; R + Python + Snakemake; has a Zenodo DOI (10.5281/zenodo.20563443) for the replication package. Updated Jul 2026, 0 stars but methodologically complete.
candidates.why_useful: Directly answers gap #17 (nowcasting with mixed-frequency data, MIDAS/DFM) applied to Mexican macro activity, which is a LatAm demand proxy for ABNB's Mexico City market; the code pattern (Banxico pull + Trends + mobility + MIDAS) is reusable for a Mexico travel-demand nowcast.
candidates.time_coverage: not stated in listing, IGAE monthly series

candidates.name: sie_banxico
candidates.what_it_holds: Python class wrapping Banco de Mexico's Economic Information System (SIE) REST API — fetch any published series (FX, rates, inflation, activity) by series ID. 4 stars, MIT, updated Jan 2026.
candidates.why_useful: One-command pull for Mexican peso FX and macro series (consumer strength / FX gap #7 and #6) at whatever frequency Banxico publishes; complements Mexico City nights forecast with a real-time peso/rate input.
candidates.time_coverage: as far back as each SIE series goes (many decades for FX/CPI)

candidates.name: banxico-api
candidates.what_it_holds: Python package to fetch Banxico economic/financial series with metadata handling and date-range queries. 1 star, MIT, updated Dec 2024.
candidates.why_useful: Alternate, actively-typed Banxico client if sie_banxico is unmaintained; same use case (Mexico FX/macro pull).

candidates.name: br_ibge_api
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client for IBGE's (Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics) open data API — consumes IBGE's 'Serviço de Dados' (municipality, geography, and statistical series endpoints). 7 stars, MIT, updated Jul 2025.
candidates.why_useful: Gives a one-command pull path for Brazilian macro/demographic series feeding gap #7 (Brazil IBGE regional travel/macro read for LatAm demand) and could support the ADR/nights regional-mix work for Brazil.

candidates.name: GET_INPC
candidates.what_it_holds: Python script pulling Brazil's INPC (consumer price index) series from the IBGE API and writing to a database. 0 stars, updated Jul 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Narrow but concrete: a working script for Brazilian CPI pull, useful for FX/consumer-strength regional split (gap #6/#7) if IBGE macro is wanted alongside BCB.

candidates.name: estatapi
candidates.what_it_holds: R package client for Japan's e-Stat API (政府統計の総合窓口), the government statistics portal covering CPI, tourism, consumption, demographics. 23 stars, actively updated Mar 2026, listed on CRAN-adjacent ecosystem.
candidates.why_useful: Most mature/highest-starred e-Stat client found; enables pulling Japanese travel/consumption/CPI series for APAC regional macro read (gap #7), and Japan is a disclosed ABNB region proxy market.
candidates.time_coverage: full e-Stat catalogue (decades for many series)

candidates.name: estat-mcp
candidates.what_it_holds: e-Stat API client plus an MCP server wrapper for Japanese government statistics. 10 stars, Apache-2.0, updated 13 Sep 2026 (very fresh).
candidates.why_useful: Actively maintained alternative Japan macro-stats client; MCP wrapper means it could be plugged into an agent workflow for repeated e-Stat pulls (tourism/consumption nowcasting for APAC gap #7).

candidates.name: estat-pandas
candidates.what_it_holds: A pandas-datareader extension for Japan's e-Stat API — pulls series directly into pandas DataFrames. 0 stars, MIT, updated May 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Lower-friction Python (vs R) e-Stat client that slots into a pandas-based nowcasting pipeline for Japan APAC macro (gap #7).

candidates.name: japan-cpi-tracker
candidates.what_it_holds: End-to-end pipeline + dashboard pulling Japan's regional CPI data from the official e-Stat API. 0 stars, updated Aug 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Regional (prefecture-level) CPI granularity could feed a Japan consumer-strength regional split, finer than national CPI.

candidates.name: korea-stats-mcp
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP server for querying Korea's KOSIS (Korean Statistical Information Service) national statistics in natural language; published as npm package @kimdayoun/korea-stats-mcp. 16 stars, MIT, updated 10 Sep 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Most-starred, freshest KOSIS client found; gives programmatic access to Korean tourism/consumption/employment/housing series for APAC regional macro (gap #7).

candidates.name: pykosis
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client to read Korea's national statistics (population, prices, employment, housing) from KOSIS OpenAPI; sibling to the author's R package `kosis` (5 stars). 0 stars but updated 10 Sep 2026 alongside the R version.
candidates.why_useful: Python-native alternative to korea-stats-mcp for direct KOSIS series pulls (housing/prices relevant to gap #13 crossover analysis too as a bonus).

candidates.name: kosis-openapi-mcp
candidates.what_it_holds: KOSIS OpenAPI CLI + MCP server with automatic period-splitting when a query would exceed the API's 40,000-cell limit. 0 stars, MIT, updated 13 Sep 2026 (very fresh).
candidates.why_useful: Handles KOSIS's cell-limit pagination automatically, useful if pulling long historical Korean series (multi-decade monthly data would otherwise need manual chunking).

candidates.name: ABS_SDMX-JSON_API
candidates.what_it_holds: Tableau Web Data Connector demo for the Australian Bureau of Statistics ABS.Stat Developer API (SDMX-JSON). 7 stars, updated Feb 2026 (likely a stale repo touched by a bot/mirror update, original code older).
candidates.why_useful: Documents the ABS.Stat SDMX-JSON query shape, transferable to a direct Python/R pull of Australian tourism/consumption series (gap #7, #6).

candidates.name: ABS
candidates.what_it_holds: Script(s) to retrieve data from ABS.Stat using the official API. 3 stars, updated Sep 2024.
candidates.why_useful: Simple working retrieval example for Australian macro series if the SDMX-JSON demo above is insufficient.

candidates.name: mcp-abs-au
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP server wrapping the Australian Bureau of Statistics Data API. 0 stars, MIT, updated 13 Sep 2026 (brand new).
candidates.why_useful: Newest ABS client found; could be plugged into an agent-driven pull of Australian tourism/travel or consumption series for gap #7, though unproven (0 stars, day-old).

candidates.name: nesstarR
candidates.what_it_holds: R package to parse NESSTAR binary survey data containers (.Nesstar files), specifically noted for use with MoSPI India survey microdata and other national statistical offices' legacy formats. 1 star, updated Jun 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Unlocks reading India's MoSPI legacy survey microdata files (household consumption/expenditure surveys) that are otherwise in an opaque binary format — relevant to gap #7's India MOSPI target and broadly to any NESSTAR-format national stats office archive.

candidates.name: Mospi Legacy Data Extraction Tool
candidates.what_it_holds: Hackathon tool ('Mospi Legacy Data Extraction Tool') to extract, digitize, and process historical datasets from India's Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI); includes a user guide in the README. 2 stars, updated Mar 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Directly targets the stated gap-7 need for an India MOSPI client, specifically for legacy (pre-digital) datasets that are otherwise hard to access; quality is hackathon-grade so treat as a lead to verify, not a turnkey tool.

candidates.name: sie_banxico_bi
candidates.what_it_holds: Python library to retrieve and visualize Mexican economic indicators via the Banxico SIE API, wrapping https://www.banxico.org.mx/SieAPIRest/service/v1/doc/consultaSeries. 1 star, updated Jul 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Another actively-touched Banxico wrapper with visualization built in; marginal over sie_banxico but confirms the SIE API pattern is well-trodden and easy to build on.

candidates.name: indicadores-economicos-mexico
candidates.what_it_holds: Full pipeline: Banxico API -> Python/pandas -> SQL Server -> FastAPI (JWT) -> Power BI/Excel, for Mexican economic indicators. 0 stars, updated Jul 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Shows a more production-grade ETL pattern around the Banxico API if the team wants a database-backed refresh rather than ad hoc scripts.

notes: No usable repos found for Colombia DANE, Argentina INDEC, or Chile stats-office clients: the combined OR query only returned MOSPI India hits, meaning gh's search treats a multi-clause OR loosely and/or there is genuinely little GitHub activity around DANE/INDEC APIs (dead end for this pass; someone should retry with dedicated single-term searches like 'dane api colombia python' and 'indec argentina python' since those got crowded out this round given the 6-call budget). Mexico INEGI got zero hits on 'inegi api python' specifically (INEGI's own API is less commonly wrapped than Banxico's; try 'inegi python' or 'datamexico' or 'INEGIpy' by name in a follow-up). All 22 candidates here are acquisition-method repos (official government-statistics API clients/wrappers), not committed datasets — consistent with the theme ("...clients"). Quality signal is generally low (most are student/portfolio projects with 0-20 stars); the one standout is thisisZAQ/nowcasting-mexico, a genuine MIDAS/DFM nowcasting replication package with a Zenodo DOI that fits gap #17 directly. Recommend a human spot-check sie_banxico, br_ibge_api, estatapi, korea-stats-mcp as the most mature single client per country before building a pull script on top of any of them. Did not use gh api / WebFetch inspection calls given the 6 gh-search budget was the binding constraint and most results are self-descriptive from README titles; a follow-up pass could verify these clients actually still work against live endpoints (government APIs change ID schemes / require app keys that can lapse).
